Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients with signs or symptoms of heart disease.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient has a documented history of recurrent severe myocardial infarctions and coronary artery disease, indicating clear signs of heart disease.

Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients selected because of either medical or research interest to the Principal Investigator.
Inclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient's severe heart issues and genetic factors like the LDLR mutation make him a prime candidate for research interest.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Patients must not have unstable angina pectoris, unstable course following recent (within one month) myocardial infarction.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient's last heart attack was over two years ago, so he does not have recent unstable angina or myocardial infarction.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: Must not be in New York Heart Association functional class IV heart failure.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient's heart failure is classified as Stage III, which is not class IV.

Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Criterion: A positive pregnancy test will obviate any cardiovascular testing requiring ionizing radiation.
Exclusion_Criteria_Evaluation.Justification: The patient is male, so this criterion does not apply.

Recap: The patient meets all the inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria.
